title: Le Monde: ownership and control
summary: Le Monde is a French national newspaper and digital news publication. Its publisher, Société éditrice du Monde, is 72.5% owned by Le Monde libre and 25.4% by the Pôle d’indépendance. The Fonds pour l’indépendance de la presse indirectly controls the majority holding. Separate shareholder and journalist governance rights are documented below.

gaps: The reported stakes total 97.9%. The remaining 2.1% was not identified; no shareholder identity is inferred.
The June 2026 disclosure reports Prisa’s 2025 exit but a pending challenge to the transaction’s corporate resolutions. Prisa is omitted from current ownership edges.
The same disclosure reports one share retained through Xavier Niel’s NJJ Strategy. Its precise issuing entity is unclear, so no equity edge is assigned.
The fund’s April 2024 acquisition announcement establishes its ownership of NJJ Presse, but a full current capitalization table for Le Monde libre was not obtained.
The fund’s statutes and About URLs opened without usable substantive text. Current founder appointment powers were therefore not independently verified from opened page content.
The governance page displayed a relative modification date. Undated appointment observations use null rather than a guessed date.
Recent ownership searches found the June 2026 disclosure; no subsequent completed sale was established.
All findings are unreviewed. Wikidata identifiers were not verified.
